name: LDL/HDL cholesterol ratio
rangeNote: There is no universal app range for this ratio; a laboratory range is used when supplied. Interpretation depends on the separate cholesterol results and overall heart risk. The app records reported ratios only and does not silently calculate them from LDL and HDL results.
summary: This ratio is LDL cholesterol divided by HDL cholesterol, with both values in the same units. It describes their relative amounts, not your overall heart risk. A lower ratio does not mean that high HDL cancels the risk from high LDL.

high.meaning: A higher ratio means more LDL relative to HDL and is associated with higher cardiovascular risk in studies. Discuss a result outside your laboratory's range with your doctor; the separate LDL, HDL and triglyceride results still matter.
commonCauses: A combination of higher LDL and lower HDL

low.meaning: A lower ratio means less LDL relative to HDL, but is not a guarantee of low heart risk. High HDL alone can lower the ratio without lowering LDL; the absolute LDL value and other risk factors still matter.
commonCauses: Lower LDL cholesterol, including during cholesterol-lowering treatment
A combination of lower LDL and higher HDL

sources.title: Lipoprotein ratios: Physiological significance and clinical usefulness in cardiovascular prevention
